safety_verdicts.content: Headache is still present at the time of consultation.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states the headache is still present at consultation; Generated does not explicitly state persistence at time of consult.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting that the headache was still ongoing at the time of the consult can reduce clarity about acuity and response to any interventions, but it is unlikely to directly change immediate management in an otherwise stable headache presentation. The main impact is loss of clinical detail for follow-up comparison.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold documents no neck stiffness; Generated does not mention neck stiffness.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Neck stiffness is a key red-flag symptom in febrile headache (e.g., meningitis/subarachnoid processes), so failing to document its absence weakens safety-netting and risk stratification. Although the underlying fact is negative, omission can lead to either missed reassurance or inappropriate escalation depending on downstream interpretation.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold documents no fever; Generated does not address fever.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Fever status materially affects the differential diagnosis and urgency of evaluation for headache (infectious and other secondary causes). Omitting that fever was denied (per gold) reduces the reliability of the clinical picture and could affect triage or follow-up decisions.
